verdictRationale: All pass criteria are met. Jaina thinks and argues with herself on the page in every scene, in her own idiom. The five speakers are distinct. No limited-third violations were found. Dialogue is grounded. Texture is 94.3/100, and all 13 beats are dramatized through concrete moments. The findings below are sentence-level and advisory. Finding 1 (a flooding-hull image at the ward cutoff) sits in the style guide's forbidden drowning family and should be fixed before the slop stage, but one simile is not enough to fail the chapter.

resolved: Opening no longer replays Ch1's 'Start talking'; it opens from the order already given ('She had been talking since before dawn; she could talk a while longer').
Texture went from 67.5 to 94.3. Compound dropped from 23.6% to 9.4%, and participial rose from 4.2% to 9.5%.
The B8 surfacing-from-deep-water image is gone.
'No. Slower.' now appears once (B12). 'That was all' appears once, and 'her face did nothing at all' appears once.
'Noticed' filter verbs are gone, and so is the 'It didn't need to' narrator punchline.
The B7 statement of the elves' experience as fact is now speculative ('might have been sitting in a quiet room... and never known it').
'Not on the hill' is now paid off at B12 ('Last night on the hill there had been nothing to see at all'), which is a strong fix.
Paragraphs over 100 words fell from 30 to 13.
A '###' hard cut now sits before B11.
carriedOver: The B7 drowning image was swapped for a flooding hold, which is the same image family (finding 1).
The Lyriel/Cyndia glance template is still used twice, nearly verbatim (finding 3).

findings.passage: Out here there was nothing to follow at all. It pressed in from every side at once, the way a hold fills when the hull's stove in.
findings.problem: Iteration 0 flagged a drowning image at this beat. The revision replaced it with a ship's hold flooding through a stove-in hull. That is still overwhelm rendered as water rushing in to sink you, the family the style guide forbids ('Drowning metaphors for overwhelm'). The swap kept the image and changed only the vehicle. It also lands on the chapter's biggest perception beat, where a forbidden image is most visible.
findings.fix: End the sentence at 'It pressed in from every side at once.' The plain statement is strong after 'thread' and 'cable'. If the beat needs Jaina's sea idiom, use one with no water coming in, such as a ship caught aback with the wind from every quarter at once. Do not use flooding, sinking, surfacing or water closing over anything.

findings.passage: She wanted to go down. She wanted, very badly, not to. She wanted somebody else to choose between them. She was angry with herself for wanting that, and it was a long way from the first time today. ... Jaina hated it exactly as much as she had at the Pass. She was glad of every one of them, too, and she hated that rather more.
findings.problem: The chapter's close leans on one move three times in nine paragraphs: she wants something and dislikes wanting it ('she'd have hated him for it', 'angry with herself for wanting that', 'hated that rather more'). B12 makes the same move too ('she hated that—hated it'). The voice sheet sanctions this move, but stacking it here names the emotion (wanted, angry, hated, glad) where the plan asks dread to 'settle flat'. The tail of 657 ('and it was a long way from the first time today') is a narrator wink from outside her, not her thought.
findings.fix: In 657, end the paragraph at 'She wanted somebody else to choose between them.' Windrunner then chooses in the next two paragraphs, so the wish is answered in action, not commentary. Keep 663, because its 'Cargo again' callback earns it, and keep the Antonidas line in 655, which is her characteristic unfairness to him. If 663 still feels heavy, cut its last clause to 'She was glad of every one of them, too.'

findings.passage: She glanced across at Cyndia. Cyndia was checking her own girth and didn't look round. The ranger seemed perfectly satisfied with that. / Lyriel glanced across at Cyndia. Cyndia was watching the hedge and gave no sign of having heard a word. Lyriel looked entirely pleased with that, settling back in her saddle.
findings.problem: This is the same three-sentence template, Lyriel's glance, Cyndia's non-reaction and Lyriel's satisfaction, used twice. It is Lyriel's voice-sheet tell, but the second use reads as a copy of the first rather than a callback. Iteration 0 flagged it, and it is unchanged.
findings.fix: Keep the first, which introduces the tell. At 367, use the other half of Cyndia's sheet, where she answers a joke with a task. Lyriel glances across, and Cyndia, eyes still on the hedge, says something like 'Watch your side.' Lyriel's satisfaction then goes unstated or gets a single beat. That shows the pair's dynamic instead of repeating it.

findings.location: Scene 2, B10, end of the first-farm sequence (line 409)
findings.passage: "Nobody leaves a good milk cow to bawl like that," Lyriel said, close at her knee, low. "Not unless they mean to be home by milking, or else they—"
findings.problem: This is the third statement of the same inference in fifteen lines: Cyndia's 'I'd say they meant to come back to it', then Jaina's 'somewhere they meant to come back from' / 'Or they hadn't gone anywhere they could come back from', then Lyriel. It adds nothing new. Livestock knowledge is also Neral's lane, and she already had the cow line at 385. The drop-back mid-sentence is Lyriel's tell and works well. The content is what repeats.
findings.fix: Keep the mid-sentence drop-back but give Lyriel something new. Her sheet says she asks real questions because she wants the answers, so she could ask Jaina about the staff or what the kitchen felt like ('You went white at that doorway. What's in there?') and drop back before Jaina can answer. That would also seed her later 'what does it taste like' curiosity.

findings.passage: Windrunner didn't look round. She didn't say *go on*, either. Jaina went on. / She didn't look round. She didn't say *better*, or *that's more like it*, or any of the things a tutor says...
findings.problem: The 'She didn't look round. She didn't say *X*' construction opens two paragraphs 36 lines apart within one exchange. The second is the one that matters, since the tutor's missing praise is the payoff, and the first one blunts it.
findings.fix: Change 317 so the payoff construction is used only once at 353. For example: 'Windrunner rode on with her back to her. Jaina went on anyway.'

findings.location: Discovery beats: B6 (line 133), B7 (line 207), B12 (line 565); also lines 35, 381, 619
findings.passage: "Oh, Light," she said, very quietly. / Light. Oh, Light. / Light. That was the interesting part. / ...Light help her (x3)
findings.problem: 'Light' is Jaina's sanctioned oath, but nine uses in 13k words, three of them opening a paragraph at a discovery beat, make it the default way a discovery lands. 'Light help her' appears three times verbatim.
findings.fix: Keep B7's 'Light. Oh, Light.' as the biggest hit. At B12, start the paragraph at 'That was the interesting part.' The line is sharper without the oath. Vary one of the three 'Light help her' lines; 381 can go, since 'It was in the cabbages, as it had been in the hawthorn' carries itself.

findings.passage: "Then the question is whether Millhaven is the source or the sink," she said.
findings.problem: 'Source or sink' reads as modern physics jargon, and her voice sheet warns against making her sound like a modern scientist. Her next sentences use the plainer verbs anyway ('If it's rising there... If it's draining there').
findings.fix: Match the line to the words that follow: 'Then the question is whether it's welling up at Millhaven or draining into it.'

findings.passage: Windrunner took her hand off the wall, straightening. Jaina watched her come up off her heels and turn her chin a fraction toward the door
findings.problem: This is a blocking glitch. Windrunner was standing and leaning a hand on the wall, not crouched, so 'come up off her heels' after 'straightening' suggests a squat that was never staged.
findings.fix: Drop 'come up off her heels', for example: 'Jaina watched her turn her chin a fraction toward the door, like a slack line coming taut on a cleat.'

findings.passage: like taking hold of a sheet with the wind already in the sail / like a rail on a pitching deck / like a door slammed on a crowded room / the way a hold fills... / like a hand over an ear / as if the road had iced over / as her father's crews knew weather by the gulls
findings.problem: Comparisons now run at about 3.3 per 1000 words (about 20 'like a', 11 'as if', plus comparative 'the way'), down from 5-6 but still above the style guide's 1-3 band. The B6-B7 stretch is densest, with roughly seven comparisons in about 90 lines. Most are in Jaina's sea/lab domain and are good individually.
findings.fix: Cut two or three in B6-B7. The best candidates are 'like a rail on a pitching deck' (135), 'as if the road had iced over under them' (213) and the hull image (finding 1). Keep the sail, the gulls and the hand-over-ear motif, because those carry the ward thread.

findings.passage: The gate rangers dragged the bar back. They rode out under the white-blue lamps and down... / It sat at the bottom of a long, shallow fold of land where two roads crossed...
findings.problem: Participial phrases are 9.5% against a 12% target (dimension score 77), the only dimension below 100. This is advisory only, since the overall score passes. The scorer's flagged telegram runs are mostly deliberate: the 'Hold/Clear' roll call, 'Hot horse. Tired horse. Clean blood.', and the B3 admission. They should stay.
findings.fix: If a later pass touches these paragraphs, convert a few finite-verb joins into ', Ving' phrases in transit and landscape narration, not in dialogue or the fight. For example, at 309: 'Jaina's hand came back slowly, first the pins, then the burn...', or at 635: 'a stream running along the bottom of the fold under a stone bridge, turning nothing'.

findings.passage: It was the second doe, the one that had been behind the leader... She stumbled. She came on. (109 words / 8 sentences) / It was the most interesting thing she'd found since the first stone... and nobody knocking. (113 words / 8 sentences)
findings.problem: Thirteen paragraphs still exceed 100 words, against 30 before. Most are within tolerance or are briefing speech (343 is Jaina's full-register explanation, which the exception covers). Line 469 is an action paragraph, where the guide wants a shorter baseline. The Terenas-hunt memory slows the half-second it sits in.
findings.fix: Split 469 after 'like a sack of meal off a cart.' so that 'This one hadn't dropped.' opens its own paragraph and hits harder. Line 567 can stay as one movement.

checkSummaries.emotionalLife: Pass. Jaina argues with herself in every scene. Scene 1 has the Antonidas/stone self-correction ('Caution, a good apprentice's caution—oh, Light, no'). Scene 2 has the B9 recalibration ('It had been a fair guess... It had not been a fair guess'). Scene 3 has curiosity against decency over the doe and the wait-for-light dilemma at the overlook. Registers include comic (the stockings, Lyriel's ice joke and the Ranger-Lord laugh, the stomach as a first-year), warm ('someone had kept up'), exhausted, horrified and dreading. Every value shift lands on a concrete moment: the hands stopping mid-air at B9, the frost fern, Cyndia's 'Slowly', the doe's hot belly.
checkSummaries.voiceAndRegister: Pass. Rhythm matches the anchor's long-then-short pattern. 'Said' stays invisible. Paragraph shape is varied, and narration carries Jaina's cadence and scholar's idiom (sums, column, next test, bench).
checkSummaries.limitedThird: Pass. No omniscient intrusions. Other characters' states are read through behaviour or offered as Jaina's (mis)read, such as the quartermaster/crucible look at B8. Sylvanas's stone knowledge stays hidden behind her 'narrower' stillness at B4, which is good dramatic irony that does not leak.
checkSummaries.dialogueRegister: Pass. No institutional or clinical vocabulary. Sylvanas is clipped and exact, with a full sentence when she lays out the map logic. Cyndia reports in event order with her view last ('I'd say they meant to come back to it'). Lyriel jokes in the flat-exaggeration shape. Neral speaks in horse terms and addresses Jaina once, by title. Forms of address are all per constraint. Minor: 'source or the sink' (finding 7).
checkSummaries.beatPlanFidelity: Pass. All 13 beats are present and dramatized. B4's 'listens harder' lands as physical narrowing. B8's liability read lands through the look. The B9 break happens at B9 and not earlier, and the misread is held through 'Let her count her costs'. B12's 'holds the company' lands through the ranger cordon and 'not one of them had said hurry'. B13 ends on the planted question. Constraints check: grain is not named, no undead column, no warmth between Jaina and Sylvanas, no counted time, and the pebble is consistent with Ch1.

summary: The revision is a strong, publishable-register chapter. Jaina's interior argument drives every scene, the five voices are distinct, the B9 recalibration lands on a concrete image (her hands left holding nothing), and texture went from 67.5 to 94.3. It passes. What remains is sentence-level polish: one flooding-hull image still in the forbidden drowning family at B7, a triple-stacked 'wanted it, hated wanting it' close at the Millhaven overlook, and a few repeated templates (the Lyriel/Cyndia glance, 'She didn't look round. She didn't say X', 'Light' as the discovery beat).
